title: Why every sink has a U-shaped pipe

beats.text: Every sink in your house hides this weird U-shaped pipe. Here's why.
Imagine the pipe went straight down to the sewer.
Water drains fine. But the sewer is full of gas.
And with nothing in the way, it comes straight up into your bathroom.
So we bend the pipe into a U.
After every wash, a little water stays trapped in the bend. About five to ten centimetres.
beats.label: WATER SEAL

beats.text: That water is a plug. Gas can't get through, but your sink still drains.
But a big rush of water can suck that plug right out of the U.
The fix? A pipe that goes all the way up to your roof.
beats.label: VENT PIPE

beats.text: It lets air in behind the water, so the plug stays put.
That's the pipe you see sticking out of roofs. It also lets the sewer gas out, way above your head.
The first version was S-shaped, invented in 1775. Many places now ban it, because it sucks itself dry.
One more thing. If a drain goes unused for weeks, that water evaporates, and the smell comes back.
The fix is free. Just run the tap for a few seconds.
And if you ever drop a ring down the sink, it's probably sitting in the U. You can unscrew it.
Which one did you know? Tell me in the comments. Next: why your windows have two panes.
